title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Best Practices, Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary

This playbook consolidates Applied ML standards for the eval harness, prompt sets and benchmarks, model onboarding, quality guardrails, quantization profiles, and regression triage. It is intended for ML engineers, applied researchers, and SREs operating Redwood Inference’s inference stack. The goal is consistent model quality, repeatable benchmarks, and a fast, low-friction path to diagnose regressions and remediate issues.

Scope

- Eval harness architecture and required artifacts
- Prompt set creation and benchmark conventions
- Model onboarding checklist and gating criteria
- Quality guardrails (metrics, thresholds, alerting)
- Quantization profile guidance and verification steps
- Regression triage playbook with roles and runbook steps

Owners and Contacts

- Primary owner: Applied ML Platform (engineering)
- On-call contact (eval infra): eng-sre/eval-harness-oncall
- Escalation: Head of Applied ML: Miguel Torres

Goals and Success Criteria

1. Every model that enters serving has a certified eval report and passing guardrails.
2. Regression detection latency < 4 hours from deployment for high-traffic routes.
3. Quantized variants meet defined quality delta budgets (see Quantization Profiles section).
4. Onboarding time from PR to gated rollout <= 3 business days for standard models.

Components and Definitions

- Eval harness: Automated framework that runs deterministic prompt suites, collects outputs, computes metrics, and stores results in the eval DB.
- Prompt set: Curated list of inputs with expected behaviors and metadata (domain, intent, difficulty, tags).
- Benchmark: Aggregated metrics (accuracy, relevance, safety, repetition, latency) computed over a prompt set.
- Quality guardrails: Pass/fail rules and soft warnings applied to benchmarks and production signals.
- Quantization profile: Collection of configuration parameters (bitwidth, per-channel vs per-tensor, backend flags) with expected accuracy impact.

Onboarding checklist (Model Owner)

1. Create model onboarding proposal (PRD-style) with architecture, expected cost, and intended routes.
2. Add model to eval harness registry with config: model_id, tokenizer, max_seq, padding policy, and test seeds.
3. Provide at least three representative prompt sets: dev, safety, and customer-simulated. Each prompt set must include:
   - 100+ examples for dev coverage (20% edge cases)
   - Explicit labels for expected behaviors or acceptability criteria
   - Metadata: domain, language, reproducibility tag
4. Run baseline eval: record metrics, latency P50/P95, and failure modes.
5. Define guardrail thresholds and recommended quantization profiles.
6. Review by Applied ML team and two reviewers listed in PR.
7. Approve gating and schedule canary rollout with evaluation hooks.

Prompt Sets and Benchmarking Standards

- Naming convention: <model_id>.<promptset>.<purpose> (e.g., llama2-13b.dev.general).
- Prompt metadata fields (in CSV/JSON/YAML): id, text, expected_label(s), difficulty, tags, seed.
- Coverage targets: lexical diversity > 0.65 (Shannon entropy proxy), at least 5 domains for multi-domain models.
- Benchmarks to compute by default: Exact Match (if structured), BLEU/ROUGE where relevant, embedding-similarity (cosine) for relevance, toxicity/safety scores, hallucination proxy (factuality heuristics), and latency breakdown.
- Baseline generation: always run baseline on both FP16 and primary quantized profile; capture delta metrics.

Quality Guardrails (SLOs and Thresholds)

- Critical metrics (must pass): Safety (toxicity rate) <= 0.5% on safety prompt set; hallucination rate increase <= 1.5x baseline; critical regression on intent accuracy <= 2% absolute drop.
- Soft alerts (warning): Latency P95 increase > 20% vs baseline; perplexity change > 10% on dev prompts.
- Production monitors: sample 1k responses/day per major route and run guardrail checks; any critical guardrail fail triggers immediate rollback procedures.

Quantization Profiles and Verification

Profiles are labeled and versioned in the quantization registry. Each profile must include a text description and the following attributes: bitwidth (8/4), per-channel bool, activation-quant bool, backend flags. Recommended default profiles:

- profile_f16_baseline: FP16 baseline for latency/cost comparison.
- profile_q8_per_channel: 8-bit per-channel symmetric; expected quality delta <= 1% across core dev set.
- profile_q4_compressed: 4-bit groupwise + activation quant; expected delta <= 3% for recommendation routes only.

Verification steps for a quantized candidate:
1. Run full eval harness on dev + safety + customer-simulated prompt sets.
2. Compute delta vs FP16 for all pass metrics and ensure within profile budget.
3. Run adversarial safety pass (10k synthetic safety perturbations) and check toxicity/regression.
4. Run stress perf test: sustained QPS 2x expected for canary during limited window.
5. Submit profile for review and sign-off; record canary rollout recipe.

Regression Triage Playbook (Incident-style for model regressions)

Severity levels:
- Sev1 (critical): Major production route showing critical guardrail failure (e.g., safety breach, severe accuracy drop).
- Sev2 (high): Notable metric regressions impacting SLA or customer experience but not safety-critical.
- Sev3 (minor): Small metric drift or localized issue.

Initial detection and notifications:
1. Monitor or eval harness detects guardrail breach -> automatic PagerDuty alert to Applied ML on-call.
2. Triage within 60 minutes: confirm signal, reproduce failing examples, snapshot model and config.

Triage steps (owner: Applied ML + SRE)
1. Reproduce: Run failing prompt set against current and previous deployed model to confirm delta.
2. Isolate: Determine whether regression is model, tokenizer, quantization, or serving runtime-induced (compare logs, kernel flags).
3. Remediate options: rollback to previous model/version; apply emergency filter or prompt-level workaround; adjust quantization flags; or quick micro-patch to tokenizer handling.
4. Canary strategy: If rolling forward, use 1% traffic canary with tight evaluation hooks for 24 hours.
5. Postmortem: Create incident doc within 3 business days with root cause, timeline, and follow-up actions.

Data collection and artifacts required for triage

- Eval harness result snapshot (JSON export) for the failing job.
- Raw failing prompts and outputs for both baseline and current model.
- Serving logs with kernel flags, device placement, and memory utilization.
- Quantization profile used and any transformation scripts.

Operational runbook snippets

- Run eval harness locally (example):
  export EVAL_ENV=staging
  python -m eval_harness.run --model-id <model_id> --promptset <promptset> --output /tmp/results.json

- Compare outputs (example CLI):
  python -m eval_tools.compare --baseline /tmp/baseline.json --candidate /tmp/results.json --report /tmp/diff.html

- Canary rollout config (example YAML fragment):
  route: /chat/generate
  canary:
    weight: 0.01
    duration: 24h
    evaluation_hooks: ["eval-harness-callback", "sampled-production-checks"]

Governance and Review cadence

- Quarterly audit: All active models must have a refreshed eval report every quarter.
- Release gating: No model may be promoted to global traffic without passing onboarding checklist and approval from Applied ML and two reviewers.
- Post-deployment: 72-hour elevated monitoring window with daily evals for canaryed models.

Appendices

Appendix A: Example prompt set metadata CSV header
  id,text,expected_label,difficulty,tags,seed

Appendix B: Minimum eval harness job spec (YAML)
  job_name: <model_id>-baseline
  model: <model_id>
  prompt_sets: [dev, safety, customer_sim]
  metrics: [accuracy,relevance,toxicity,latency]
  environment: staging

Appendix C: Quick checklist for on-call when alerted
1. Acknowledge PagerDuty and check eval harness job status.
2. Gather artifacts listed above.
3. Reproduce with smallest failing promptset.
4. If Sev1, coordinate rollback immediately and notify product & legal if safety-related.
